main_text.p: 3.habent signa, quibus bonos a malis discer-nant, in amicis vero judicandis nullas habent. Sunt igitur firmi. Primum praeceptum de amicitia constituenda est, ut eligamus constantes & firmos. Constantia autem exploranda primo tempus exponit: quod incidit in ipsam amicitiam: idque confirmatur ab effectu amicitiae: illa enim praecurrit judicium, tollitque potestatem experiendi. Deinde modum describit duobus similibus, quorum prius petitum est a stadii cursoribus, alterum ab aquis. Sensus est: Ut qui stadium currunt seipsos cohibent: sic in amicitia cursum affectuum refraenare & cohibere debemus: & ut aquam, antequam plenius hauriamus, primis labris degustamus: sic animorum mores prius probabimus, actum demum amabimus.

p.i: Tertio subjectum, in quo amicorum mores periclitandi sunt, triplex proponit, pecuniam, honores, pericula: qui enim in tribus i-stis nihil praeter constantiam admiserit, eum vere constantem judicare possumus. Propo-nuntur autem tria illa gradatione quadam logica, quae a minoribus ad majora procedi-tur. Difficile est amicitiam anteponere pe-cunia, difficilius honori, difficillimum peri-culu[?]

page.notes: The page begins mid-paragraph, so the first paragraph is marked as continuing. The numeral "3." at the start is printed in the running text and is kept as printed. Italic is used for most of the text; the phrases "Sunt igitur firmi." and the roman passages are set in roman. The paragraph break before "Tertio" is a judgment: the line above is full, and the word begins at the margin, so the break is inferred from the sense rather than from indentation. The last word is broken at the line end as "peri-" / "culu", and the final letter is uncertain at the scan edge. Italic and roman boundaries in the first lines are approximate.
